items.sentence: Revenue rose 167.4% in FY2023 to $4.43 billion , which the filing ties to higher deliveries and average selling prices .

passages.filing: FY2023 10-K Item 7. Management's Discussion and Analysis
passages.text: Revenues increased primarily due to an increase in deliveries of 29,790 vehicles, increased average selling prices, and sales of non-Rivian vehicle trade-ins. Included in revenues for the year ended December 31, 2023 was $73 million of regulatory environmental credit sales.

items.label: supported
items.reason: Passage states revenue increase due to higher deliveries and average selling prices.

items.sentence: Volkswagen Group revenue of $836 million  contributed 15.4pp of FY2025 growth , and the filing ties software growth to joint-venture development services .

passages.filing: FY2025 10-K Item 7. Management's Discussion and Analysis
passages.text: Software and services revenues increased significantly for the year ended December 31, 2025 primarily due to an increase in vehicle electrical architecture and software development services, as well as increases in remarketing sales and vehicle repair and maintenance services.

items.label: partial
items.reason: Passage supports software growth from development services but not Volkswagen revenue contribution.

items.sentence: Automotive revenue fell 14.6% in FY2025 , a -13.2pp contribution to growth , as deliveries declined .

passages.filing: FY2025 10-K Item 7. Management's Discussion and Analysis
passages.text: Automotive revenues decreased for the year ended December 31, 2025, primarily resulting from a decrease in deliveries of 9,332 vehicles, due in part to the expiration of 45W tax credits after September 30, 2025, as well as a decrease in sales of automotive regulatory credits, partially offset by higher average selling prices and a higher mix of R1 deliveries. The increase in average selling prices was driven by a consumer shift towards higher performance variants along with a decline in discounting.

items.label: supported
items.reason: Passage states automotive revenue decrease due to lower deliveries.

items.sentence: Automotive gross losses improved on higher average selling prices and lower cost per vehicle , with cost of revenue down 15.0% .

passages.filing: FY2025 10-K Item 7. Management's Discussion and Analysis
passages.text: Automotive gross profit losses improved for the year ended December 31, 2025, primarily due to the higher average selling prices and reductions in the cost per vehicle noted above.

items.label: supported
items.reason: Passage attributes improved gross losses to higher prices and lower cost per vehicle.

items.sentence: Operating cash outflow fell from $1.72 billion in FY2024  to $779 million , which the filing ties to a significant reduction in net loss .

passages.filing: FY2025 10-K Item 7. Management's Discussion and Analysis
passages.text: Net cash used in operating activities decreased during the year ended December 31, 2025 compared to the year ended December 31, 2024, primarily driven by a significant reduction in net loss.

items.label: supported
items.reason: Passage states decrease in cash used in operations driven by reduced net loss.

items.sentence: Capex of $1.71 billion  was 2.18x D&A  and 31.7% of revenue , which the filing ties to Normal Factory capacity expansion .

passages.filing: FY2025 10-K Item 7. Management's Discussion and Analysis
passages.text: Net cash used in investing activities decreased during the year ended December 31, 2025 compared to the year ended December 31, 2024, primarily driven by lower purchases of short-term investments, partially offset by lower maturities of short-term investments and higher capital expenditures related to the expansion of production capacity at our Normal Factory. During the year ended December 31, 2025, we continued to invest in the growth of our business at our Normal Factory, our next generation vehicle platforms and technologies, and our go-to-market infrastructure.

items.label: partial
items.reason: Passage ties higher capex to Normal Factory expansion but not the specific ratios.

items.sentence: Financing inflows of $886 million  came mainly from Volkswagen Group share issuance , and the 2031 notes refinanced the 2026 Notes .

passages.filing: FY2025 10-K Item 7. Management's Discussion and Analysis
passages.text: Net cash provided by financing activities during the year ended December 31, 2025 primarily resulted from the issuance of $750 million in shares of Class A common stock to Volkswagen Group in connection with the achievement of the Financial Milestone, as well as capital contributed by outside parties in the formation of Mind Robotics, Inc. and Mind Robotics, LLC (see Note 1 "Presentation and Nature of Operations" and Note 19 “Variable Interest Entities” to our consolidated financial statements included in this Form 10-K for more information). Net cash provided by financing activities during the year ended December 31, 2024 primarily resulted from the issuance of the 2026 Convertible Note (see Note 10 “Debt” to our consolidated financial statements included in this Form 10-K for more information).

passages.filing: FY2025 10-K Item 7. Management's Discussion and Analysis
passages.text: In June 2025, we issued approximately $1.3 billion aggregate principal amount of fixed rate senior secured green notes due January 15, 2031 (“2031 Green Secured Notes”) in a private offering to qualified institutional buyers pursuant to Rule 144A under the Securities Act and outside the United States to non-U.S. persons pursuant to Regulation S under the Securities Act. The 2031 Green Secured Notes were issued pursuant to an indenture dated as of June 12, 2025 (the “Indenture”). The proceeds were primarily used to redeem in full the $1.3 billion aggregate principal amount of the 2026 Notes.

items.label: partial
items.reason: Passage supports Volkswagen share issuance and refinancing, but not the exact financing inflow figure.
